raw_case_text: A 15-year-old boy, presented with a right leg swelling, which increased in size over 2 months. There was no history of fever or weight loss. Radiograph of right lower limb showed a lytic sclerotic mass in proximal meta-diaphysis of right fibula, which on biopsy was suggestive of Ewing's sarcoma. Whole body 18F-fluoro-deoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG PET/CT) was performed as a part of staging work-up. Maximum intensity projection (MIP) image [Figure 1a] showed intense focus of tracer uptake in the right leg (arrow) and liver (arrow-head). Axial fused PET/CT images revealed intense tracer uptake in destructive lytic-sclerotic soft tissue mass in upper end of right fibula, with a maximum standardized uptake value (max SUV in milliCurie/kilogram of body weight) of 7.8. An intense solitary focus of FDG uptake was seen in hypodense lesion in caudate lobe of liver [Figure 1c - arrow], which was presumed to be metastatic on the basis of imaging findings. It measured 16 mm in transverse dimensions with a max SUV of 8.2. Rest of the study was unremarkable, except for reactive mediastinal nodes. Subsequently, patient underwent induction chemotherapy for 6 weeks. Follow-up FDG PET/CT study after treatment completion showed complete regression of tracer concentration at primary site in tibia on MIP image [Figure 1b - arrow], as well as reduction in size of the soft tissue mass with post treatment healing changes in the fibula seen on axial CT images. Contrary to this, the focal hepatic lesion in caudate lobe of liver showed significant increase in size and metabolic activity [Figure 1b - arrow head]; measuring 31 mm, with max SUV of 14.6 on axial fused PET/CT images [Figure 1d - arrow]. This prompted a histological correlation and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) was done from the liver lesion. Microscopic examination showed collection of epitheloid cells on Papanicolaou Stain [Figure 2a - arrows and Figure 2b] with pale oval shaped cells showing slipper shaped nuclei [Figure 2b - inset]. These findings were confirmatory for tuberculous etiology. Patient was immediately started on antituberculosis treatment, and follow-up is awaited.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 15-year-old boy presented with a right leg swelling that had enlarged over 2 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 15-year-old boy presented with progressive swelling of the right leg over 2 months. Lower limb radiography and biopsy of the proximal meta-diaphysis of the right fibula established a primary diagnosis of Ewing sarcoma. Staging whole-body FDG PET/CT revealed a hypermetabolic caudate liver lesion presumed to be metastasis. He completed 6 weeks of induction chemotherapy, after which repeat PET/CT showed response in the fibular lesion but paradoxical progression of the hepatic lesion.
subjective.past_medical_history: Proximal right fibular Ewing sarcoma diagnosed on biopsy; status post 6 weeks of induction chemotherapy. No prior tuberculosis history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Denied fever, weight loss, or other systemic complaints. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Right leg swelling corresponding to fibular mass. Remainder of physical examination normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Plain radiograph of right lower limb: lytic-sclerotic mass in proximal meta-diaphysis of right fibula.
objective.advanced_workup: Staging whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT: intense tracer uptake in right fibula destructive mass (max SUV 7.8) and solitary hypodense lesion in caudate lobe of liver measuring 16 mm (max SUV 8.2); reactive mediastinal nodes. Post-chemotherapy PET/CT: complete metabolic regression of primary fibular mass with bone healing changes, but interval enlargement of caudate lobe liver lesion to 31 mm with increased metabolic activity (max SUV 14.6). Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of liver lesion: collection of epithelioid cells on Papanicolaou stain with pale oval-shaped cells and slipper-shaped nuclei.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Hepatic tuberculosis mimicking metastatic disease in a patient with Ewing sarcoma, confirmed by liver fine-needle aspiration cytology demonstrating epithelioid cell collections with characteristic slipper-shaped nuclei on Papanicolaou stain diagnostic of tuberculous etiology. Primary Ewing sarcoma demonstrated complete metabolic response to 6 weeks of induction chemotherapy while the hepatic lesion progressed due to untreated tuberculosis. Management & Outcome: Initiated immediately on antituberculosis treatment; ongoing clinical monitoring maintained.
